post.description: Profile's "Confirm your email" prompt, for accounts older than the code step.

Start a password reset. ALWAYS returns 200, whether or not the email is
registered — never reveal which addresses have accounts. If it exists, a
single-use, short-lived token is stored (hash only) and a reset link emailed.

Revoke the presented refresh token. Idempotent and always 200 — it must
not reveal whether the token existed.

delete.description:
Permanently delete the account — required by App Store review, and the
right default for a privacy product: no soft-delete, "deleted" means deleted.

Re-confirm with the password, or the word DELETE for an account with none
(deletion is irreversible). ORDER MATTERS: the
recordings live in external storage the DB cascade knows nothing about, so we
enumerate and delete every audio object FIRST (while the rows still tell us the
keys), THEN delete the user — whose cascade removes entries, todos, topics,
people, and refresh tokens. Getting this backwards orphans every recording in
the bucket forever.

schema.description:

get.description:
Mint a short-lived signed URL for an entry's recording.

Authenticated and ownership-checked (404 for non-owners — a user must not be
able to tell whether someone else's entry exists). Returns {"url": ...}; the
CLIENT fetches the audio bytes directly from Supabase Storage with that URL,
so we never proxy (and never pay egress for) the audio.

This closes the old auth gap: the previous route streamed bytes with no token
because <audio> can't send an Authorization header. Now an authenticated call
mints the URL and the media element loads *that*.

post.description:
Throws an unsaved entry away, with its recording and its waiting AI actions. The month's
entry count isn't given back: the recording was already transcribed and read.

With an answer: the AI carries on from its question (free, at most MAX_ANSWERS). Without:
the step runs now that the user allowed AI actions (one request of the allowance).

existing one by toName). An optional alias — the surface form being split off —
is attached to the target so future mentions of it read as ambiguous.

get.description:
The user's todos across every entry, soonest-first.

`?done=true|false` filters by completion; omit it for everything. Timed items
(startAt) and dated items (dueDate) come first in chronological order, then
undated ones. Each carries its source entryId so the client can link back.
